newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: ATHLETICS-LEWIS SAYS DRUG LOOPHOLES MUST BE CLOSED.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-LEWIS SAYS DRUG LOOPHOLES MUST BE CLOSED.

text.p: American track and field star Carl Lewis said on Thursday that some countries were still defending drug-tainted athletes and loopholes must be closed to keep the sport clean.

"I think there is definitely an effort to make the situation better, but I also think everyone has to come to the table, and there are still loopholes that need to be closed," Lewis said in New Zealand, where he will run the 100 metres in a meet in Auckland on Friday.

"There are still countries that fight for their athletes even though they know they're dirty, and I don't think that's going to change until everyone has a consensus and everyone refuses to accept the situation that people are on drugs," he told Radio New Zealand in an interview.

The nine-time Olympic gold medallist said drug cheats were "doing different things than they were doing three years ago", and the sport's administrators had to keep pace. Current loopholes included training camps where athletes were not available for testing.
Lewis, 35, confirmed 1997 would be his final year of competition and that he had "completely retired" from the long jump to concentrate on the 100 metres.

"This is my last year, and I wanted to take this year to kind of go to some of the places that I hadn't visited before. It's an opportunity for me to exhibit myself in places that I haven't been before and also a lot of places that have been very nice to me," he said.
Lewis said that after retiring, he would concentrate on promoting physical fitness and pursuing an acting career.
Did he plan to become a movie star?

"Well, we'll see. I'm in a situation where I can really do what I want to do for the rest of my life. Financially I'm in a position to call all my own shots, so I'm going to do the best I can," Lewis said.

"We'll see -- if it happens and it works out great, that'll be tremendous, but if it doesn't, I can accept that. At least the challenge of trying to do something very, very difficult and very challenging is there."
